bullets.title: Nasdaq worst week since June as AI unwind accelerates; SOX down 8 straight sessions
bullets.body: Nasdaq fell 4.48% for the week, its worst performance since June, with the SOX index down 11.4% and DRAM sector off 18.8%. Semis logged 8 consecutive losing sessions—tied for the longest streak since 2006—as financing concerns, ROI visibility questions, and China competitive pressure (CXMT 4F² DRAM claims) drove a historic rotation. Equal-weight S&P outpaced cap-weighted by 225bps, the largest such outperformance since November 2020.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure financing stress: CRWV CDS hits record, Anthropic valuation trimmed to $1.5T
bullets.body: CoreWeave CDS spreads spiked to a record ~1,194bps implying >60% default probability, with the stock down ~27% from early October. Anthropic Q3 annualized revenue of ~$74B came in below the $100B investor target, prompting valuation cuts from $2T to $1.5T. Gartner warned $3.5T of AI infrastructure is at impairment risk by 2030, with 80%+ of neocloud providers expected to fail. Goldman notes all 2025 net HF buying of Global AI has been reversed.

bullets.title: Fed on hold in October; December and March hikes remain 'strong baseline' as core CPI runs hot
bullets.body: September core CPI printed +0.33% m/m vs. 0.2% consensus, pushing October hike odds as high as ~45-50% before Warsh's noncommittal IMF remarks pulled them back to ~15-16%. Morgan Stanley, JPM, and multiple independent macro shops all see December as highly probable and March as likely. Core PCE is tracking ~0.33% m/m with year-over-year expected at ~3.07-3.25% underlying. September PPI was sharply above consensus at +0.7% m/m core.

bullets.title: AI capex estimates surge even as financing cracks widen: MS raises to $1.6T in 2027, JPM to $400B+ for top-4 CSPs
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its top-9 CSP AI capex estimate ~14% to $1.6T (+60% y/y) in 2027, rising to $1.8T in 2028. JPM lifted cloud DC capex for top-4 to +85% in 2026 and +70% in 2027, with $400B+ in absolute 2027 additions. AI investment now exceeds 60% of SPX+neocloud capex and is estimated to lift S&P 500 sales growth by ~200bps. Meanwhile credit markets are bifurcating sharply—IG hyperscalers resilient, HY neoclouds under severe stress with USD HY AI spreads widening 25bp+ in one session.

bullets.title: Hedge fund de-grossing reaches 3-sigma: Info Tech largest net selling on record, Health Care net bought fastest in 7 months
bullets.body: GS Prime reports Info Tech saw the largest percentage net selling on record (since 2016) and the biggest de-grossing in two months over the Oct 9-15 period. Overall HF book saw -2.0 SD net selling. TMT L/S funds are down 5.1% MTD but still up 12.6% YTD. Offsetting, Health Care was net bought at the fastest pace in seven months driven by short covers. Net leverage fell to 72.7%—4th percentile vs. the past year.

bullets.title: Retail sector breadth rotation: defensives, energy, staples outperform as AI/momentum unwinds
bullets.body: XLP outperformed the S&P by ~476bps WTD (cumulative 2-week ~760bps, 6th best in 10 years). Energy and utilities led within S&P while software/cybersecurity lagged. Real estate REITs outperformed the broader index +1.15% vs. S&P -1.95% on the week. Retail dip-buying recovered to $5.4B/day in October, +28% from September, with SOXL ETF seeing $3.2B in two sessions.

bullets.title: September IP surges to 49-month high; utilities and high-tech industries lead AI-driven demand
bullets.body: September industrial production rose +0.7% m/m vs. +0.4% expected—a 49-month rate-of-change high. High-tech industries jumped +1.49% m/m and +17.6% y/y (highest since Feb 2011). Utilities surged +3.5% m/m as AI-related power demand strengthened. Semiconductors within IP rose +2.0% m/m. Morgan Stanley and Piper Sandler both noted broad manufacturing strength.

bullets.title: TSMC raises FY26 guide to +44% y/y; N2 capacity to more than double in 2027; CEO open to Terafab collaboration
bullets.body: TSMC posted Q3 revenue of $46.7B above the $45.4B consensus and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B vs. $50.1B street. FY26 revenue growth guidance was raised to +44% from +40%. HPC was 68% of Q3 wafer revenue; N2 represented 8% and is on track to more than double capacity in 2027. CEO noted agentic AI is driving CPU demand well beyond prior estimates, and 2026-2028 aggregate capex will significantly exceed the prior three years.

bullets.title: Agentic AI disrupts OTA distribution: META Muse completes travel bookings independently, OTA stocks down 15-25%
bullets.body: Meta's Muse and Instinct agents now complete full travel booking cycles including payment via browser automation, bypassing OTA platforms entirely. Google has rolled out hotel booking inside AI Mode. OTA stocks fell 15-25% following these launches. None of the 11 tracked platforms (4 OTAs, 7 hotel chains) has built systems allowing outside agents to complete bookings independently. The dynamic is viewed as deflationary for OTA commissions, positive for hotel brands and consumers.

bullets.title: SpaceX acquires 800 MHz low-band spectrum; telco stocks lose $50B+ in market cap on Starlink wireless threat
bullets.body: SpaceX agreed to acquire 800 MHz of low-band spectrum from Grain Management, raising competitive fears across AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile. The three carriers lost approximately $50B in combined market cap. Morgan Stanley views the selloff as overdone and reiterates OW on T and TMUS, noting SpaceX would need significant infrastructure buildout to compete; 5K equipment deployments on CCI towers by 2028 could hypothetically uplift CCI EBITDA 7.5%.

bullets.title: Q3 S&P 500 earnings blended growth at 29%; 84% beat rate above averages but surprise magnitude weak
bullets.body: Q3 blended EPS growth is tracking 29.0% y/y (slightly below 29.6% expected at quarter-end) with 84% of reporters beating—above the 82% one-year and 78% five-year averages. Revenue beat rate of 67% is below the 77% one-year average. Earnings surprise magnitude of +2.6% is well below the 13.8% one-year and 7.5% five-year averages, suggesting a raising-the-bar dynamic. This marks the 8th straight quarter of double-digit EPS growth.

bullets.title: Oil at new highs targeting $120; Gulf of Oman flows drop 20%; Middle East risk premium elevated
bullets.body: WTI crude hit new cycle highs with a $120 price target cited by multiple strategists. Flows out of the Gulf of Oman declined to 13.5 Mb/d from a 17 Mb/d early-October peak. Iranian strikes on Strait of Hormuz shipping are ongoing, tanker attack frequency has risen from ~4 to ~11/week, and Saudi Arabia's full-year 2026 GDP forecast was trimmed 0.3ppt to -2.6% by JPM on Houthi attacks. Diesel tightness is spreading into gasoline.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasuries posted best week since February as AI risk-off drives flight-to-safety; 5.08-5.10% after touching 5.36%
bullets.body: Treasuries rallied sharply as the AI infrastructure unwind triggered a rotation toward safety. The 10-year yield fell 16bps to ~5.08% on the week after briefly trading near 5.36% following the hot CPI print. The 2s/10s curve steepened. JPM technical analysis sees 5.15-5.25% as the Q4 yield floor for the 30-year; MOVE Index elevated at 102 but off highs.

bullets.title: Midterm elections Nov 3 a key AI infrastructure catalyst: 35+ data center ballot measures across 8 states
bullets.body: More than 35 data center-related ballot measures will appear on November 3 ballots across 8 states, with Ohio accounting for over 50%. Governor races in Ohio, Texas, and Georgia carry direct implications for data center permitting, grid interconnection, and moratorium risk. A Virginia senator has proposed a 3-year data center moratorium. Analysts note near-term regulatory uncertainty as an overhang for the sector.

bullets.title: AAPL iPhone Duo preorders surge; delivery slipping to late January as demand outstrips supply
bullets.body: Apple's iPhone Duo (foldable) preorders launched October 16, with delivery timelines extending to late January—interpreted as strong initial demand. Apple closed above $5T market cap briefly. However, iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max production cuts of ~15% were flagged by multiple channel checks as an early headwind to the bull case. AAPL shares traded +2% premarket on launch day.

bullets.title: Accenture Investor Day sets first-ever multi-year targets: MSD growth FY27-28 accelerating to mid-to-high single digits in FY29
bullets.body: ACN issued its first formal 3-year revenue guidance at its Investor Day, calling for mid-single digit constant-currency growth in FY27-FY28 accelerating to mid-to-high single digits in FY29—well above street. Operating margin expansion of 10-30bps annually and FCF/NI of 1.1x+ were also guided. AI-related bookings tripled, agentic commerce pipeline reached $1B, and the Network of Businesses segment (currently 6% of revenue) is expected to double to 12% by FY29. Stock rallied ~25% following early October earnings.

bullets.title: Retail sales surged +6.3% YoY in September; consumer spending resilient despite inflation squeeze
bullets.body: September retail sales beat at +0.8% m/m headline (vs. +0.3% consensus), with the YoY rate reaching +6.3% overall and +4.5% ex-gas. Consumer electronics rose +8.8% YoY, sporting goods +9.1%, and eCommerce +7.9%. Major bank card data corroborated the strength: JPM +10%, WFC +9.2%, Citi +10.7% YoY. However, US gas prices at +40% YoY and real hourly earnings negative for 3 consecutive months represent growing pressure on lower-income cohorts.

bullets.title: CTA models signal $2.5B supply in RTY and $1B in NDX; systematic leverage remains a tail risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley QDS flagged that CTA models show potential $2.5B supply in Russell 2000 futures and $1B in NDX over the coming week. Macro systematic leverage remains high, meaning any correlated move lower could trigger significant additional supply. Implied correlation on SPX members remains very low (<10% for 1-month expiry), which QDS says is mispricing tail risk. Asset managers are the most short VIX futures on record.

bullets.title: TSLA unveils flying Roadster at SpaceX event; Morgan Stanley and MS industrials analysts turn more constructive
bullets.body: Tesla unveiled a new Roadster with SpaceX thruster capability targeting 230+ mph and 0-60 in under 1 second at an event Thursday, driving shares up ~3-5% in premarket. The event also featured ~300 Cybercabs now deployed in Austin with 1M+ unsupervised miles accumulated. Morgan Stanley's auto analyst Andrew Percoco turned 'more constructive' post-event, citing peak negativity having passed and robotaxi density as the key 2026 catalyst.

bullets.title: Frontier AI lab ARR threshold of $400-500B critical to justify capex; real risk is a 'capex winter,' not an 'AI winter'
bullets.body: 22V Research framed the key debate: frontier labs need $400-500B in annualized recurring revenue exiting 2027 to justify current capex at 15% ROIC through 2028-2029. Hyperscaler FCF consensus over five years totals over $700B, potentially disproving the negative CapEx thesis if AI revenue materializes. The real risk cited across multiple shops is a capex slowdown (flat hyperscaler spending), which would pressure NVDA growth, reprice neocloud debt, and weaken picks-and-shovels valuations—not an end to AI adoption.
